http://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/27922.text: Big News Network.com Two trains smash into each other in Croatia, dozens injured At least 20 people were injured when a commuter service collided with a freight train, according to the Health Ministry At least 20 people were injured when two trains collided in Croatia on Saturday, the country's Health Ministry has said. The incident occurred shortly after 10am between the Sveti Ivan Zabno and Gradec railway stations, around 60km east of the Croatian capital, Zagreb. A passenger train carrying 27 people collided with a freight train, leaving six people seriously injured and 14 others with minor injuries. The victims were taken to hospitals in Bjelovar and Koprivnica, with some later transferred to medical facilities in Zagreb. A young woman was placed in intensive care but remained in stable condition. Videos posted online show the wreckage, with passengers sitting and standing beside the railway. The passenger train appears heavily damaged, with its roof buckled and exterior panels torn away. Red freight wagons and a locomotive can be seen ahead. One photo shows part of the passenger train bent at a sharp angle near the point of impact, with a shattered cab windscreen and twisted handrails. Koprivnica-Krizevci County Prefect Tomislav Golubic expressed gratitude to the 50 firefighters involved in the operation, as well as to a civilian who assisted with the rescue effort. "I would especially like to thank a local man for arriving first at the scene with his personal forklift, making it easier for emergency services to tend to the injured," Golubic said. Damir Loncaric of Croatian Railways said an investigation into the collision was underway. Deputy Prime Minister Tomo Medved, who later visited the site, praised emergency workers for their response. He said preliminary information indicated that either a technical failure or human error could have caused the crash but stressed that the final determination should be left to the competent authorities. The accident came five days after a passenger train struck a trailer carrying hay at a level crossing in Tczew County, northern Poland. Around 500 people were reportedly on board at the time. Polish State Railways said the tractor driver had ignored warning signals and was found to be intoxicated. Photograph: Central News View image in fullscreen Nicholas Brandram was arrested in June in connection with a 2017 incident in which a jogger running across Putney Bridge pushed a woman towards an oncoming bus. Photograph: Central News UK news Suspect in ‘Putney pusher’ case found dead at his west London home HSBC director Nicholas Brandram, 44, was found unresponsive by emergency services on Tuesday evening Vikram Dodd Police and crime correspondent Wed 16 Sep 2026 13.53 EDT Last modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 16.41 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A senior city banker suspected of pushing a woman into the path of a moving bus in the “Putney pusher” case has been found dead. Nicholas Brandram, 44, was discovered at his home in Chiswick, west London , on Tuesday. He was arrested in June by the Metropolitan police in connection with a 2017 incident in which a jogger running across Putney Bridge pushed a woman towards an oncoming bus . She only avoided serious injury after the driver swerved around her at the last moment. Brandram was a director at HSBC and had previously served in the military, reaching the rank of captain. He was released on bail by detectives in June after being arrested on suspicion of attempted grievous bodily harm. In September, after answering bail, he was re-bailed with no conditions. Video footage showed the woman being pushed by a male jogger. She fell into the road, with the jogger running on. The Met wound down its investigation in 2018, after interviewing 50 men and arresting three suspects. The case, which attracted considerable attention, was unsolved. In a statement on Wednesday, the Met said: “At 19.12 on Tuesday, 15 September officers and the London ambulance service attended an address in Chiswick, Hounslow after a man was found unresponsive inside a property. “Sadly, a 44-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene. His next of kin have been informed. “At this time his death is being treated as unexpected, but is not believed to be suspicious. “A file will be prepared for the coroner in due course.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines UK Get the day’s headlines and highlights emailed direct to you every morning after newsletter promotion Brandram was the grandson of Princess Katherine of Greece, who was the great-granddaughter of Queen Victoria, the Daily Telegraph reported in 2013 when he was convicted of crashing his Harley-Davidson motorbike into a female cyclist around Hyde Park Corner, before driving off without leaving his details. In an interview with the Citywealth website in March this year, Brandram said he was a senior relationship manager at HSBC Private Bank. He said: “I usually bicycle into our office in Mayfair from my home in west London. And then from there, can either stay at my desk, go to Canary Wharf or the City, or get on a train or go to the airport. My first meeting is ideally over breakfast and I’m ideally home for bath time. I’m a co-parenting single father with a three-year-old.” Brandram said his proudest professional achievement was being invited to a Buckingham Palace garden party after military service in Afghanistan, and that the person he most admired was his mother. “She raised three children as a single parent and is the busiest person I know,” he said. “I’ve never met someone with greater moral integrity and courage, as well as resilience and stamina.” Explore more on these topics UK news London news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland

https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story.text: NATO fighter jets have shot down a drone that entered Lithuanian airspace overnight, officials say, less than a day after NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said that strikes close to the alliance's territory would drive the trans-Atlantic organisation to increase its support for Kyiv. The drone was downed near the village of Pratkunai in the Kaisiadorys district, about 100km west of the country's capital, Vilnius, and near the Kaunas Reservoir, Lithuania's National Crisis Management Centre said on Tuesday. Lithuania's military said the incident marked the first time that a drone had been shot down in the country's airspace. Authorities did not comment on the drone's origin or purpose, saying the incident needed further investigation. The incursion follows a speech by Rutte on Monday at NATO headquarters in Brussels, where he said that strikes "close to NATO territory" showed Russian President Vladimir Putin's "desperation and also his desire to sow fear and terror". "Russia is growing increasingly reckless as it continues its terrible war against Ukraine," Rutte said. He also pledged to bolster the 32-nation alliance's own defences along its long eastern border with Russia. The menace of drones has repeatedly loomed over the skies of Lithuania, which shares borders with Belarus, a key ally of Moscow, and the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. Antanas Matutis, commander of the Lithuanian air force, said that the wreckage had been found, and the drone "likely" was carrying explosives. Vilmantas Vitkauskas, head of the crisis centre, told Lithuanian public broadcaster LRT that the drone most likely entered from Belarus. It remained in Lithuanian airspace for about 30 minutes and flew along the outskirts of populated areas before being intercepted, he said. In a separate encounter between Russian and NATO forces on Tuesday, Denmark's foreign ministry said a Danish air force helicopter had been fired upon with flares in connection with "routine photographic coverage" of a Russian frigate in waters off the port of Gedser in the Baltic Sea. "This is completely unacceptable," the ministry wrote on X, saying that the Russian ambassador was summoned over the incident. Meanwhile, Russian drone strikes continued across Ukraine following a social media post from US President Donald Trump on Monday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed "not to hit" each other's energy infrastructure. Trump did not offer further details on the purported agreement, and Russia did not immediately comment on Trump's post. Previous efforts to broker even a partial ceasefire have repeatedly fallen apart within hours, with both sides accusing each other of violations. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said late on Monday that Kyiv was "ready to support de-escalation" if the United States could ensure "Russia is genuinely ready to stop this war". But Zelenskiy said on Tuesday that Moscow had continued to attack Ukraine's energy sector, logistics and critical infrastructure, and Kyiv had responded by striking an oil refinery in Syzran, a city in western Russia. "There is no alternative to ending this war. And all forms of pressure on Russia must create the right diplomatic conditions," Zelenskiy said. Ukraine's State Emergency Service said on Tuesday that Russian strikes on Kyiv had killed one person and wounded seven other people since the start of the day, with attacks carried out on the capital's gas stations. Another two people were killed in separate Russian strikes in the Ukrainian cities of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said. Elsewhere, Russian forces shot down 222 Ukrainian drones overnight, Russia's defence ministry said. A "massive" Ukrainian drone attack sparked several fires in the Russian city of Taganrog, regional governor Yuri Slyusar said. He said on Telegram that two apartment buildings and three private homes had been damaged, as well as an educational institution, agricultural warehouses and a site belonging to Russian e-retailer Ozon. Zelenskiy said on Tuesday that Kyiv's forces had targeted a drone production facility in the city. Australian Associated Press
